title: One-word / overly short answers
note: Students can learn to immediately add a reason, detail, or example.

title: Overusing basic connectors
note: Can be improved by practicing a small set of natural alternatives and varied sentence structures.

title: Repetitive basic vocabulary
note: Replacing a few high-frequency words with precise alternatives produces quick gains.

title: Obvious filler words
note: Awareness + repeated practice can quickly reduce “um,” “uh,” “basically,” etc.

title: Memorized / robotic openings
note: Stop using scripts and practice multiple natural openings.

title: Overly formal / essay-like language
note: Students can learn conversational alternatives relatively quickly.

title: Too much unnecessary detail
note: Mostly a matter of learning when to stop and practicing concise responses.

title: Simple pronunciation errors
note: Individual recurring sound errors can often be isolated and practiced directly.

title: Weak word stress
note: Can improve through repeated listening, marking stress, and imitation.

title: Poor sentence chunking
note: Shadowing and chunking exercises can produce noticeable improvement.

title: Weak use of basic grammar structures
note: Repeated spoken practice can automate common patterns.

title: Weak tense consistency
note: Particularly manageable in familiar narratives such as Part 2.

title: Weak collocations
note: Students need both knowledge and repeated contextual use.

title: Limited topic vocabulary
note: A relatively straightforward knowledge problem, but requires substantial exposure.

title: Weak paraphrasing
note: Requires vocabulary flexibility rather than simply memorizing synonyms.

title: Difficulty describing something without the exact word
note: Requires developing circumlocution/recovery ability.

title: Weak answer organization
note: Frameworks like A.R.E. and P.E.E.P. help, but students must learn to use them flexibly.

title: Weak Part 2 development
note: Requires learning to generate details, events, feelings, and reflection spontaneously.

title: Weak Part 3 development
note: Students need to learn explanation, examples, qualification, and opposing perspectives.

title: Weak idea generation
note: The problem isn't necessarily English; students have to learn how to generate content quickly.

title: Difficulty discussing unfamiliar topics
note: Requires flexible thinking and the ability to speculate rather than relying on prepared knowledge.

title: Grammar errors while speaking spontaneously
note: Students may know the grammar but cannot retrieve it accurately under pressure.

title: Slow lexical retrieval
note: Requires substantial repetition before vocabulary becomes automatic.

title: Translation from L1 → English
note: Changing the underlying processing habit takes time.

title: Slow processing/formulation
note: Multiple mental processes have to become faster and more automatic.

title: Excessive self-correction
note: Students must change how they monitor themselves while speaking, not simply learn more English.

title: Poor spontaneous flexibility
note: Requires being able to transform known language/content under changing questions.

title: Difficulty handling follow-up questions
note: Requires real-time listening + thinking + responding + adapting.

title: Weak interaction/repair skills
note: Students have to recover naturally from communication problems rather than simply produce prepared speech.

title: Unstable fluency under cognitive pressure
note: Fluency can collapse when vocabulary, grammar and ideas are simultaneously demanded.

title: Part 3 abstract thinking weakness
note: This involves reasoning, generalization, comparison, qualification and perspective—not just English.

title: Severe pronunciation/rhythm problems across connected speech
note: Requires long-term perceptual and motor adjustment rather than simply memorizing rules.

title: Performance collapse under pressure
note: The student may know the language but cannot access it reliably in an evaluative environment.

title: High speaking anxiety/fear of mistakes
note: This can interfere with nearly every other speaking skill at once.

title: Deep lack of automaticity
note: Knowledge exists, but the student cannot deploy it quickly enough during real-time speech.

title: Fundamental low speaking ability
note: When vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation, processing, confidence, and exposure are all weak, there is no single quick intervention.
